question: I didn’t really understand the reason that our gullible heroine, Beako, had, in the past, rejected people who had tried to take her away, and Subaru in the on-the-way loops, but in the final loop, she responded fondly to him. What on earth was the deciding factor there?
answer: It’s because he laughed off Beako’s insistence on being hung up on ‘that person’ as silly, and had Beako choose ‘the best’. All the people up to that point had not known about ‘that person’, or on the other hand even if they did know, they were the type to say ‘I’ll become that person’. Hence, they couldn’t overcome Beako’s internal priority for the ‘Command from Mother’. In Subaru’s case, he handed the right to choose to Beako, and Beako herself broke down the order of ‘Subaru’ > ‘that person’ > ‘Command from Mother’. I’m sorry I wasn’t able to depict that very well. You should apologize too, please, for not being able to pick it up from reading.
